newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Draka, Twentsche Kabel sold cross shareholdings.
newsitem.headline: Draka, Twentsche Kabel sold cross shareholdings.

text.p: Dutch cable makers Draka Holding NV and NV Twentsche Kabel Holding said on Monday they had sold the shareholdings the companies held in each other.
Draka owned 11 percent of Twentsche Kabel and the latter had a 5.5 percent stake in Draka.

The shares were sold through investment bank Kempen & Co to investors in and outside the Netherlands at last Friday's closing prices of 79.00 guilders per Draka share and 102.00 guilders per Twentsche Kabel share.
The proceeds will be used for the expansion strategies of both companies, Draka and Twentsche Kabel said in a joint statement.
The cable makers said they had previously taken the cross shareholdings to strengthen their cooperation in the area of buying raw materials.
"Both parties think the cooperation can also be continued without owning interests in each other's share capital," Draka and Twentsche Kabel said.

Before the start of trading on Monday, the Amsterdam bourse said it had suspended trading in Draka and Twentsche Kabel, pending an announcement. The bourse later said trading in the shares would resume at 1210 GMT.
